To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a vector space-based model for selectional preference prediction can be trained from a combination of a large syntactically annotated corpus and a small semantically tagged corpus; 2) this combination yields better performance than a model trained from the syntactically annotated data alone; and 3) our model is able to capture inverse selectional preferences.

(i) a corpus-based vector space model for selectional preference prediction can be successfully applied to both regular and inverse selectional preferences; (ii) it is possible to train the model using a combination of a semantically annotated primary training corpus and a syntactically annotated generalization corpus; and (iii) the model can be applied to a variety of NLP and cognitive tasks.
